description:
Remove the unqualified `satisfies:<id>` coverage form so every coverage credit names the container whose criterion it satisfies, and nested containers can reuse criterion ids without crediting each other.

## Background

`label_credits_id` in `crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs` accepts three label shapes: the qualified `satisfies:<container-short-id>/<id>`, the structural `satisfies:@/issue/<id>/<kind>/<id>`, and the legacy unqualified `satisfies:<id>` (`None => value == id`). `label-coverage` walks the whole dependency subtree, so an unqualified label on a story's child also credits the same-numbered criterion of every enclosing container. A consuming repository hit this while planning an epic with two nested stories: the stories' children carried `satisfies:REQ-01..10` for the story criteria and falsely credited the epic's REQ-01..10, which forced a manual renumbering of the story criteria to REQ-21..27 and REQ-31..40. The qualified form already scopes credit correctly; only the unqualified arm causes the collision.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `label-coverage` and every other coverage-crediting path credit a criterion only through the qualified or structural form; an unqualified `satisfies:<id>` label credits nothing.
- [hard] REQ-02: An unqualified `satisfies:<id>` label is reported by validation with a message naming the qualified replacement, so consuming repositories find every label to migrate.
- [hard] REQ-03: The unqualified matching branch and the tests that pin its crediting behavior are removed; the qualified and structural behavior suites still pass.
- [hard] REQ-04: Templates, skills, bundled profiles, documentation and examples in this repository emit and describe only the qualified form.
- [hard] REQ-05: A coverage fixture with an epic and a nested story that both declare `REQ-01` shows each container credited only by labels scoped to it.
- [hard] REQ-06: A `jit issue batch-create` manifest can credit a container created in the same manifest by referring to that container's manifest key in a qualified coverage label, which resolves to the created container's short id; the breakdown skills and templates use it, so a story and the tasks that satisfy its criteria are created in one manifest.

## Notes

The migration of existing unqualified labels in consuming repositories is their own work; this issue covers the engine, its bundled content, and the diagnostic that finds labels to migrate. The change follows the canonical-cutover invariant: the superseded form is removed rather than kept as a compatibility path.

## Decisions

- D-1: REQ-06 was added by the owner in session 8: the qualified-only cutover must not regress single-manifest breakdowns that create a story with its satisfying tasks.
title: Remove the unqualified satisfies coverage form
